diagnosis.what_happened: Document headings were left left-aligned because the regex matching was too narrow (only matching section numbers) and QC scripts falsely reported success using a document-wide string check.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: Strict regexes missed top-level titles, and the coarse QC check failed to catch the absence of alignment tags on specific paragraphs.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: Exhaustive application of right alignment (<w:jc w:val='right'/> + <w:bidi w:val='1'/>) to all heading levels, followed by rigorous per-heading DOM-based validation.
diagnosis.rationale_why: Persian academic documents strictly require right-to-left orientation and right alignment across all structural elements without exception.

desired_behavior: 1) Apply universal right-alignment enforcement on ALL headings, titles, and captions (<w:jc w:val='right'/> + <w:bidi w:val='1'/>); 2) Perform per-paragraph DOM validation confirming that EVERY heading element has explicit <w:jc w:val='right'/>, strictly forbidding document-wide string containment checks.
generalization: Enforcing layout properties in RTL documents requires comprehensive targeting (not narrow regex) and granular structural validation (DOM parsing, not raw text search).
